title: Comprehensive Neuro Set 1: Autonomic Nervous System (Short Answer)

questions.prompt: Based on their anatomical origin in the central nervous system (CNS), what are the specific names given to the two primary divisions of the ANS?
questions.modelAnswer: Sympathetic and Parasympathetic.

questions.prompt: Which spinal cord segments contain the cell bodies of the preganglionic sympathetic neurons?
questions.modelAnswer: T1 to L3 (Thoracolumbar).

questions.prompt: In which specific regions of the CNS do the preganglionic parasympathetic neurons originate?
questions.modelAnswer: Nuclei of cranial nerves (III, VII, IX, X) and S2-S4 (Craniosacral).

questions.prompt: How do the lengths of preganglionic and postganglionic axons compare between the sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions?
questions.modelAnswer: Sympathetic: Short preganglionic, long postganglionic. Parasympathetic: Long preganglionic, short postganglionic.

questions.prompt: What is the classification (A, B, or C) of the preganglionic and postganglionic motor fibers in terms of conduction velocity and myelination?
questions.modelAnswer: Preganglionic fibers are myelinated B fibers; postganglionic fibers are unmyelinated C fibers.

questions.prompt: Which neurotransmitter is released by all preganglionic neurons of the ANS, regardless of division?
questions.modelAnswer: Acetylcholine (ACh).

questions.prompt: What specific type of cholinergic receptor is found on the cell bodies of all postganglionic autonomic neurons?
questions.modelAnswer: Nicotinic (N_2).

questions.prompt: Which sympathetic effector organ is a notable exception to the rule that sympathetic postganglionic neurons are adrenergic?
questions.modelAnswer: Thermoregulatory sweat glands (innervated by sympathetic cholinergic neurons).

questions.prompt: Explain the concept of "en passant" synapses and the role of varicosities in autonomic neuroeffector junctions.
questions.modelAnswer: Postganglionic autonomic neurons form diffuse branching networks with beads called varicosities, which are the sites of transmitter synthesis and release along the target tissue.

questions.prompt: What is the standard ratio of epinephrine and norepinephrine secreted by the chromaffin cells of the adrenal medulla?
questions.modelAnswer: 80% Epinephrine and 20% Norepinephrine.

questions.prompt: Which enzyme, required for the synthesis of epinephrine in the adrenal medulla, requires cortisol for its induction?
questions.modelAnswer: Phenylethanolamine-N-methyltransferase (PNMT).

questions.prompt: List two examples of "non-adrenergic, non-cholinergic" neurotransmitters released by some postganglionic parasympathetic neurons in the GI tract.
questions.modelAnswer: Vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP), substance P, or nitric oxide (NO).

questions.prompt: Which adrenergic receptor type is found primarily on vascular smooth muscle of the skin and splanchnic regions, and what is its effect upon activation?
questions.modelAnswer: α_1 receptors; they produce excitation (contraction/constriction).

questions.prompt: Describe the second-messenger signaling pathway used by α1  receptors.
questions.modelAnswer: G_q protein activates phospholipase C, which produces IP_3 and diacylglycerol, leading to increased intracellular Ca^(2+).

questions.prompt: What is the physiological significance of α_2  receptors acting as "autoreceptors" on presynaptic adrenergic terminals?
questions.modelAnswer: They inhibit further release of norepinephrine from the terminal (negative feedback).

questions.prompt: Which G protein and second messenger system are utilized by α_2  receptors?
questions.modelAnswer: G_i protein; it inhibits adenylyl cyclase and decreases cAMP.

questions.prompt: Name the primary locations of β_1  receptors and the three major effects they have on cardiac tissue.
questions.modelAnswer: SA node, AV node, and ventricular muscle. Effects: Increased heart rate, increased conduction velocity, and increased contractility.

questions.prompt: What is the common second messenger mechanism shared by all β adrenergic receptors?
questions.modelAnswer: Stimulation of adenylyl cyclase via Gsprotein, leading to increased cAMP.

questions.prompt: Which adrenergic receptor is responsible for the dilation of bronchioles and vascular smooth muscle in skeletal muscle?
questions.modelAnswer: β_2 receptors.

questions.prompt: In the cardiac SA node, what is the mechanism by which the M_2 muscarinic receptor decreases the heart rate?
questions.modelAnswer: It activates a G_i protein that directly opens K^+ channels (I(K-ACh)) and inhibits adenylyl cyclase, slowing the rate of phase 4 depolarization and hyperpolarizing the cell.

questions.prompt: Which cholinergic receptor type and signaling pathway (second messenger) are responsible for increasing GI motility and gland secretion?
questions.modelAnswer: Muscarinic (M3) receptors; Gqprotein, phospholipase C, IP3/Ca^(2+).

questions.prompt: Distinguish between the effect of sympathetic and parasympathetic stimulation on the muscles of the iris (pupil size).
questions.modelAnswer: Sympathetic (α1): Radial muscle contraction (mydriasis/dilation). Parasympathetic (M): Circular/sphincter muscle contraction (miosis/constriction).

questions.prompt: Describe the autonomic coordination required for the filling phase of the urinary bladder regarding the detrusor muscle and internal sphincter.
questions.modelAnswer: Sympathetic (β2) relaxes the detrusor muscle; sympathetic (α1) contracts the internal sphincter.

questions.prompt: Which receptor type mediates the sympathetic stimulation of renin secretion by the kidneys?
questions.modelAnswer: β1receptors.

questions.prompt: Which division of the ANS is responsible for male penile erection, and which is responsible for ejaculation?
questions.modelAnswer: Parasympathetic (erection); Sympathetic (ejaculation).

questions.prompt: Where are the primary autonomic centers for vasomotor, respiratory, and swallowing functions located?
questions.modelAnswer: Medulla oblongata.

questions.prompt: Describe the "Size Principle" in the context of motoneuron recruitment.
questions.modelAnswer: Small motoneurons have the lowest threshold and fire first, generating small force; larger motoneurons fire last and generate large force.

questions.prompt: What is the mechanism of action for the ganglionic blocker hexamethonium?
questions.modelAnswer: It is a nicotinic antagonist that blocks the N_2 receptors in autonomic ganglia but not the N_1 receptors at the neuromuscular junction.
